title: Impact-tier target selection: hard AI/ML projects, monthly goals
summary: Quarterly #1 hunter taiphung217 picks difficult, high-visibility AI/ML targets (Transformers, Ollama, PyTorch, TensorFlow, MLflow) and sets monthly goals; aims for RCE/DoS/sandbox-bypass/arbitrary file read-write impact rather than bug count. Choosing the right target is described as the most important step.

title: 1-day variant hunting: study past reports on the same project
summary: Instead of blind fuzzing, taiphung217 studies existing 1-day reports/PoCs from the same project, understands the root-cause context, then searches for similar issues elsewhere in the codebase - producing new variants or deeper flaws. MLflow bug family (auth-less artifact write, model-versions LFI, http_dataset_source RCE by kevin-mizu/haxatron/zpbrent) was his study corpus.

title: Escalate-before-report: hold primitives until max impact
summary: taiphung217 found an MLflow path traversal after ~3 days, then deliberately withheld reporting to spend 2 more days escalating to arbitrary file write and finally RCE via a file-writing feature. Discipline: report at the highest provable impact, chaining traversal->write->RCE instead of submitting the first primitive.

title: Split manual/automated hunting workflow (Joern + AFL++)
summary: Manual side: careful documentation reading to understand system behavior, then edge-case and logic-error analysis. Automated side: Joern for code queries/taint and AFL++ for fuzzing. taiphung217 also studies PoCs and past reports of other researchers to expand perspective.

title: Platform trend-following picks research direction
summary: Lyutoon (and taiphung217) treat huntr program updates - especially the MFV (model file vulnerability) initiative - as a map of where bounty money and undiscovered attack surface currently live. Platform scope changes are treated as research direction signals.

title: Docs-first source review: functionality before code
summary: winters0x64 workflow: adopt CTF mindset that bugs exist, learn how the app works via documentation, identify interesting/overlooked functionality, then read only that source. Then test edge cases and hunt bypasses for validation code/sanitizers. Duplicates are treated as evidence you are in the right area - persistence is the entry cost.

title: Fork + CodeQL Action workflow for free static analysis
summary: Fork the target repo, add a CodeQL GitHub Action workflow, and read results in the fork's Security tab - surfaces code paths and low-hanging fruit with zero local tooling or setup cost. winters0x64 uses this as his main automated aid on white-box huntr targets.

title: Fuzz malformed model files (GGUF) to find loader crashes
summary: Lyutoon's Ollama vulnerabilities on huntr came from fuzzing crafted malformed GGUF model files to trigger crashes; fuzzing is his first instinct when feasible. When an effective fuzzer isn't practical he switches to manual code audit, which catches logic flaws fuzzing misses - audited bugs often have greater impact.

title: LLM4Shell: LLM-integration frameworks as an RCE attack surface
summary: Lyutoon coined LLM4Shell - RCE vulnerabilities in LLM-integrated frameworks/apps (LangChain, LlamaIndex class). In the LLM era, integration introduces an unpredictable third-party element with new risks; presented at Black Hat Asia 2024. Combine with differential testing across DL libraries (TensorFlow/PyTorch/Paddle/MindSpore, USENIX Sec 2023).

title: Heat-map codebase hotspots: file handling, auth, memory management
summary: Start with ONE project and master it. Treat the codebase as a heat map: file handling (uploads/downloads/artifact processing -> LFI, arbitrary overwrite; MLflow LFI found via artifact operations), authentication logic (login/session -> ATO), memory management (C/C++ parsing -> buffer/heap overflow).

title: MFV hunting kit: parsing functions, extreme header values, sanitizers
summary: For model file vulnerabilities: search file-parsing functions (header parsing, memory allocation); use AFL++ structure-aware fuzzing + GDB + ASAN; look for integer overflows, unchecked array access, blind trust in header values; modify legitimate model files to test extreme header values (max/zero). Memory corruption in ML loaders concentrates where file parsing meets memory allocation.

title: Snyk-for-triage, Burp-for-web, LLM-for-bypass-brains tool chain
summary: McInerney's stack: Snyk as coarse overview (99% warnings but flags dense areas worth investigating), Burp Suite + extensions for web endpoints, and LLMs to brainstorm bypass methods/alternative approaches to security mechanisms. Matches the 2024 MLsecops podcast advice (Snyk then Burp then deep dive).

title: Archive-slip as pivot: model formats are disguised tar/zip
summary: .nemo/.keras/.gguf/.pth model files are zip/tar archives; raw extractall() gives Zip/TarSlip write-anywhere. Plain slips are auto-caught by huntr's scanner now, but remain the fastest first hop toward load-time code execution, backdoors and output tampering - chain, don't report raw.

title: Symlink archive members beat naive path filters
summary: Loaders that strip ../ sequences often still extract symlink members whose linkname points outside the extraction directory - payload files written through the symlink land at the target. Two PoC patterns published: path-traversal member renaming and SYMTYPE linkname abuse.

title: MFV payout gradient: what huntr actually pays for in 2025
freshness_note: pre-2.0 MFV economics; superseded-risk - re-verify MFV rewards under 2026-08 program status
summary: High value: .safetensors/.gguf/.keras/.joblib, load-time code execution via header/metadata abuse, backdoors/output manipulation, scanner-evading payloads (nested/encrypted/obfuscated). Medium-low: .pkl and fringe formats, plain Zip/TarSlip, DoS via oversized tensors, bugs needing extra imports. MFV beta tiers: up to $1,500 (pickle $750); later posts cite $3-4k.

title: Empirics of huntr reports: severity skew, NVD gap, fix-rate gap
freshness_note: pre-2.0 platform baseline (reports 09/2023-02/2025); NVD-gap finding still a vuln-intel design input
summary: 6,427 huntr reports (largest dataset): AI/ML OSS vulns skew High severity; CWE mix diverges from OWASP ML Top 10 (e.g., CWE-400 DoS); 44.4% of CVE-IDs missing from NVD (alert gap); 49.5% of severity-assigned AI/ML vulns unfixed post-disclosure vs 99.7% for non-AI/ML; avg review turnaround 85.7 days; AI/ML reports pay more but draw more Informative/N/A verdicts.

title: AI-slop counter-pressure: evidence bar is rising
summary: curl closed its HackerOne program Jan 2026 over AI-generated reports; invalid/duplicate rates rose to ~50-65%, triage time 8-14h per report; HackerOne launched Hai Triage (AI vs AI). Prediction: PoC/video-evidence requirements tighten, rewarding reproducible evidence-backed reports over volume.

title: AI-augmented expert workflow: comprehension + hypothesis, human validation
summary: Effective 2025-2026 hunters use AI for code comprehension (reading 50k-line JS data flows, mapping auth boundaries across microservices) and hypothesis generation, while keeping human target selection and validation. Structured exposure (MCP-based pentest frameworks; methodology-gated agent skills like Claude Code bug-bounty skill) roughly doubles methodology adherence vs unconstrained LLMs (0.971 vs 0.605).

title: Variant analysis of recent commits is AI's strongest fit
summary: Big Sleep (Google P0+DeepMind) found SQLite stack buffer underflow via reasoning about a recent commit's implications - code that had been extensively fuzzed because the fuzz harness missed the generate_series extension. Pattern: once a vuln class is known, find every instance - the same loop taiphung217 does manually with 1-day reports.

title: huntr program economics: 10x multiplier, $50k caps, monthly payouts
freshness_note: pre-2.0 OSV economics; superseded-risk from 2026-06-08 huntr 2.0 pivot (OSS program closed 2026-06-30)
summary: Critical OSV bounties cap at $50k (HF Transformers inaugural program paid $50k top); vulns affecting ML model read/write get up to 10x multiplier; maintainers have 31 days to validate; CVE assignment + day-90 public disclosure is automatic; payouts monthly on the 25th via Stripe Connect; OSV submissions closed - MFV-only as of 2026.

title: Disclosure pipeline: 31-day maintainer window, day-90 publication, MFV nondisclosure
freshness_note: page undated (source_date is a placeholder); pre-2.0 disclosure economics - OSV pipeline frozen 2026-07-31 (huntr 2.0 pivot 2026-06-08)
summary: huntr policy: maintainer gets 31 days to respond (researcher re-contacted every 7 days); unresponsive maintainers get reports manually resolved within 14 days; valid open-source reports go public day 90; informative/invalid go public immediately; MFV reports are never publicly disclosed. Researchers should time public writeups accordingly.

title: pickle.loads abuse in HF demo code (RagRetrieve CVE-2023-6730)
summary: [legacy-context] zpbrent found the RagRetrieve vuln: risky pickle.loads in Hugging Face Transformers exploitable via demo code; 9.0 CVSS, $1,500 bounty. Root-cause family (risky deserialization in AI libs) still frames current MFV work, but pickle-specific hunting is now low-value on huntr (bottom bounty tier).

title: Persistence through 'informative' rejection: refine PoC, win recognition
summary: [legacy-context] zpbrent's initial pickle report was rejected as 'informative'; refining the attack vector and delivering detailed PoCs flipped it to critical, earning two CVEs. m0kr4n3 similarly pivoted to web vectors after informative verdicts on other classes. Rejection is part of the process; impact documentation converts it.

title: Hacktivity as the real-world attack corpus
summary: [legacy-context] huntr team advice for onboarding: study the Hacktivity page (disclosed reports) to learn which attacks actually work in the wild rather than OWASP theory - the platform publishes the 100 most recent disclosed reports; per-project pages expose full history. Still the canonical corpus for 1-day variant hunting.

title: Re-hunt heavily scraped projects for overlooked deep bugs
summary: [legacy-context] hainguyen0207 found a path traversal in LOLLMS after many researchers had already reported on the project - a deep re-read of already-hunted codebases still yields bugs when others move on. Complements the new-repo-monitoring dup strategy (m0kr4n3).
